text.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
text.body_text: Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.
text.summary: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

audio.title: Trump Trilateral Summit In China, House Democratic Leadership, Anthropic IPO
audio.description: President Trump met with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together for the first time, but the meeting produced no major breakthrough as tensions remain over Ukraine, technology and Taiwan. House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to become the next Speaker and are already laying the groundwork for investigations into President Trump’s inner circle as they prepare to take control of the chamber. Anthropic begins trading publicly after the biggest IPO in history, testing how much appetite investors still have for artificial intelligence amid growing concerns about an AI bubble.

text.title: Now get out of that! How can the new James Bond film get around 007’s death in No Time to Die?
text.body_text: “James Bond will return,” says the closing title on No Time to Die, the most recent James Bond film and the final one to star Daniel Craig. It is just as well: Bond has to all appearances been vaporised by sea-launched missiles, having been infected by nanobots programmed to attack his nearest and dearest at the slightest touch.
text.summary: Was it all a dream? Has Bond been in hiding? Or will Robert Pattinson simply report to HR on his first day? Russell T Davies, David Hare and more give their takes “James Bond will return,” says the closing title on No Time to Die, the most recent James Bond film and the final one to star Daniel Craig. It is just as well: Bond has to all appearances been vaporised by sea-launched missiles, having been infected by nanobots programmed to attack his nearest and dearest at the slightest touch. No one would believe that one of the world’s most successful film series would come to such an abrupt halt, but no doubt a little reassurance helped. Nevertheless, the first order of business for scriptwriter Steven Knight and director Denis Villeneuve will be dealing with it: how to revive and re-energise a character at the heart of the action. Speculation on their best way forward has been rife, and previous examples are not hard to find. Sherlock Holmes was killed off by Arthur Conan Doyle by fighting his arch enemy Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls in the story The Final Problem, only to resuscitate him a decade later with The Adventure of the Empty House. Superman is apparently killed at the end of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, but resurrected in Justice League for the fight against Steppenwolf. Arguably the most enduring pop-culture return is Bobby Ewing’s famous shower scene in the TV show Dallas in 1986, which attempted to ensure continuity by suggesting Ewing’s death was his wife’s dream. And even Ian Fleming toyed with killing off Bond, with a climactic poison scene at the end of his 1957 novel From Russia with Love, and leaving him amnesiac and vulnerable to Soviet attack at the finish of You Only Live Twice, the last Bond novel published in Fleming’s lifetime.
